description: Why Single-Line Queuing Outperforms Multi-Line Queuing: A Markovian Perspective
summary:
Introduction Whenever you step into a bank or a grocery store, you encounter one of two queueing designs:
Multi-Line Queuing ($c \times M/M/1$): Each register or counter has its own dedicated line. Customers pick a line and wait. Single-Line Queuing ($M/M/c$): A single “serpentine” line feeds into all available counters. The person at the front goes to the next open station. While multi-line setups might feel faster because individual lines look shorter, single-line systems are mathematically superior in both average wait time and queue stability. Using Markov Chain theory and Queueing Theory, we can prove why pooling capacity eliminates systemic inefficiencies.
title: Single vs Multi Lane Waiting

description: Exploratory data analysis, geospatial clustering, and predictive machine learning models on NYC Bed & Breakfast listings.
summary:
1. Executive Summary This project analyzes Bed and Breakfast pricing in New York City through exploratory data analysis, geospatial visualization, and predictive modeling. The goal is to understand which market features shape nightly rates, where the highest and lowest price concentrations occur, and how accurately those prices can be predicted from listing metadata.
Several strong patterns emerge quickly. Manhattan dominates the upper end of the market, especially south of Central Park, while lower-priced listings are more broadly distributed across the outer boroughs. Room type, location, and listing structure all contribute meaningfully to price variation, and the dataset also shows a clear $999 ceiling that likely reflects a preprocessing cap rather than a true market boundary.
title: New York City BnB Analysis

description: A practical, modern guide to package and environment management with Conda and Miniforge.
summary:
Why Conda? Conda is an open-source package management and environment management system designed for scientific computing, machine learning, and multi-language development (Python, R, C/C++, etc.).
Key advantages of Conda include:
Isolated Environments: Every project maintains its own isolated dependency sandbox, preventing version conflicts between libraries (e.g. PyTorch 2.x vs TensorFlow 2.x). Binary Non-Python Dependencies: Unlike pip, which primarily manages Python wheels and packages, Conda can install compiled system libraries (such as CUDA runtimes, cuDNN, OpenBLAS, Graphviz, and HDF5) directly into your environment without requiring root/sudo privileges. Cross-Platform Consistency: Ensures identical dependency resolution across Linux, macOS, and Windows. Installation: Miniforge vs. Anaconda While full Anaconda includes a large bundle of pre-installed GUI tools and packages, the recommended modern standard is Miniforge. Miniforge is a minimalist, community-driven installer pre-configured with conda-forge as the default channel (avoiding commercial licensing restrictions of Anaconda’s default channel).
title: Conda Essentials: Complete Guide & Cheat Sheet

description: Guide how to use _\includesvg[ ] (image.svg)_ in $\LaTeX$
summary:
You may know the popular LaTeX package graphicx which you can use as:
\includegraphics[options]{filename} graphicx does not support svg, but there is the package called svg that does the job.
How to use the svg package: Install Inkscape
On Windows you can use winget.
winget install -e --id Inkscape.Inkscape Copy your image.svg file into your document root folder (= right next to your .tex file)
This is a minimal working example (MWE) for your .tex document:
\documentclass{article} \usepackage{svg} \begin{document} \begin{figure}[htbp] \centering \includesvg[width=0.8\textwidth]{image} \caption{Vector graphic rendered directly from SVG.} \end{figure} \end{document}

description: Comprehensive guide to European drone regulations (EASA/LBA), Open Category classes (A1/A2/A3), operator registration, and rules for scratch-built/DIY drones.
summary:
⚠️ Disclaimer These are practical personal notes and reference guidelines on the European Union / German Federal Aviation Office (LBA) drone regulations for operating Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS). Always cross-reference current national and EASA legislation before flying. Official training material: lba-openuav.de. Quick Launch Checklist Before operating any unmanned aircraft in European airspace, verify that you have completed all four prerequisites:
Remote Pilot Competency (Drone License): Proof of competence (A1/A3) or remote pilot certificate (A2). UAS Operator Registration (e-ID): Register as an operator with your national aviation authority (e.g. LBA in Germany) and affix your Operator ID (e-ID) to the aircraft. Third-Party Liability Insurance: Mandatory aviation liability insurance that explicitly covers drone operations and potential damage. Category & Class Verification: Ensure your flight envelope (weight, location, distance to uninvolved people) matches your drone class and certified category. 💡 Fast-Track for Beginners For standard camera drones and hobby operations, visit lba-openuav.de, complete the interactive online training, pass the free multiple-choice test for the A1/A3 certificate, and register as an operator in one seamless session. Core Regulatory Terms & Flight Rules Visual Line of Sight (VLOS): The remote pilot must maintain continuous, unaided visual contact with the unmanned aircraft (eyeglasses and contact lenses permitted, but no binoculars or FPV goggles alone). FPV Flights (First Person View): Permitted only when accompanied by a designated competent spotter standing directly next to the pilot, maintaining continuous direct visual sight and verbally alerting the pilot to approaching aircraft or obstacles. Maximum Take-Off Mass (MTOM): The certified total weight of the aircraft at launch, including batteries, cameras, and any additional payload. Payload: Any components or gear not strictly necessary for flight mechanics (such as gimbals, external sensors, landing gear) are considered payload. Maximum Flight Altitude: Standard flights in the Open Category are capped at 120 m AGL (Above Ground Level). UAS Operational Categories European drone regulations (Regulations (EU) 2019/947 and 2019/945) classify operations into three distinct operational risk tiers:
title: EU Drone License (LBA Proof of Competence A1/A3 & A2)

summary: Overview Why and when do we need linear regression? In a nutshell, linear regression is used to predict data that has a linear relationship. That means all the datapoints are roughly on a straight line (in 2D), resp. on a hyperplane (in 3D). Firstly, we find some expression for the linear relationship (e.g. in 2D: $y=a\cdot x + b$; where $a$ is the slope and $b$ is the y-intercept). Secondly, we use this expression to insert some data where we only know the $x$ value, but want to predict their unknown $y$ value.

While standard calculus builds an intuitive understanding of how error flows through individual connections, writing code using scalar loops is computationally inefficient.
In practice, modern machine learning libraries (like PyTorch or TensorFlow) compute updates over entire layers simultaneously using Matrix Calculus and linear algebra routines optimized for GPUs [rumelhart1986][lecun1988] .
title: Backpropagation in Matrix Calculus

summary:
Introduction This article gives a quick overview over the feedforward phase of a Neural Network.
Nodes A Neural Network is composed of interconnected Nodes (artificial neurons), conceptualized in foundational cybernetics by McCulloch and Pitts [mcculloch1943] and realized in the Perceptron by Rosenblatt [rosenblatt1958] . Each node operates as an elementary computational unit performing three sequential operations:
Multiply each input with an adaptive synaptic weight and compute the net scalar activation: $y_{in} = \sum_{i=0}^m w_i\cdot x_i$, where $m$ is the number of inputs. Process the net input value through a non-linear activation function: $y_{out}=f(y_{in})$. Transmit the output signal $y_{out}$ to downstream nodes in subsequent layers [rumelhart1986] . So, a single node pretty much looks like this:
title: Feedforward Phase
